senses.gloss:
Kairāta is the name of a snake in the Atharvaveda^1 — possibly,
but not probably, the modern Karait.
1) v. 13, 5. Cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 243

Kairātikā, a ‘maiden of the Kirāta people,’ is mentioned in
the Atharvaveda (x. 4, 14) as digging up roots for medicinal use.

Kairiśi, ‘descendant of Kiriśa,’ is the patronymic of Sutvan
in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (viii. 28).
